takeaway: Chest drain safe triangle: pectoralis major (front), latissimus dorsi (behind), nipple level (below); mid-axillary line at the 5th space guides. Not the mid-clavicular line (needle decompression).

lines.text: A 35-year-old man with a haemothorax needs a chest drain. Which landmark is least useful?
lines.say: A thirty-five-year-old man with a haemothorax needs a chest drain. Which landmark is least useful?

lines.text: In front: the inferolateral border of pectoralis major.
Behind: the anterior border of latissimus dorsi.
Below: the axial plane at the level of the nipple.
The mid-axillary line at the 5th intercostal space can guide the incision.
lines.say: The mid-axillary line at the fifth intercostal space can guide the incision.

lines.text: But the mid-clavicular line should not be used for a chest drain: that's the answer.
It is used for needle thoracocentesis in a tension pneumothorax.
lines.say: (clears throat) It is used for needle thoracocentesis in a tension pneumothorax.
